decisive_spans.text: brownish macules on the hands and feet
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

response.rationale: D6 (Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome) is strongly supported by the presence of brownish macules on the hands and feet, onychodystrophy, multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa, and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum. D7 (Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome) is a strong contender due to the presence of numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum and multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa, but it contradicts the presence of brownish macules on the hands and feet, which are a hallmark of Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome. The other candidates are less supported or contradicted by key findings.
